note: c_Aug sets for the two concept axes CA-LoRA contrasts.
v3 replaces both axes with the paper's own sets, quoted verbatim from
arXiv 2503.22172 Appendix B.2. The v1/v2 sets were our own reconstruction,
written before the appendix was checked; reproduction fidelity wins over a
set we designed ourselves (user decision, 2026-07-28).
IMPORTANT — these templates carry no {caption} placeholder. The paper's c_Aug
is a rewrite of the *fixed* training prompt ('photorealistic first-person
urban street view'), not a suffix appended to a per-image caption, so the
whole prompt is replaced. This couples the augmentation file to
data.caption_template: with a per-city caption the c_Aug would no longer be a
minimal edit of c and L_Concept would measure the caption difference too.
configs/sdxl_cityscapes.yaml therefore pins the fixed prompt (Table 12).
ConceptAxis.render still calls str.format(caption=...), which is a no-op on a
template without placeholders — the code path is unchanged.
Known caveat, to be settled by measurement rather than by argument: the
'eye-level view' viewpoint template agrees with Cityscapes, which is entirely
first-person, so it pulls the condition towards the real images and can cancel
against the other slots in the within-axis mean E[ghat_viewpoint]. The paper is
immune because it only ever uses CA, a norm; our direction metrics are not.
direction_concentration (||E[ghat]|| / CA, free from values already stored) is
the check: if the viewpoint axis reports a concentration near the 1/sqrt(n)
random-direction floor on the A100 measurement, cos_of_means for that axis is a
cosine between two cancelled-out vectors and must be read with that in mind.
augs_per_sample=4 still draws without replacement from the 5 templates.
